title: Simon Boccanegra
subtitle: Domingo, Haroutounian, Calleja · Levine
summary: Off-air recording of the Metropolitan Opera's live Saturday matinee radio broadcast of Verdi's Simon Boccanegra on 9 April 2016 (Toll Brothers-Metropolitan Opera International Radio Network), with James Levine conducting Plácido Domingo (Boccanegra), Lianna Haroutounian (Amelia), Joseph Calleja (Gabriele Adorno), Ferruccio Furlanetto (Fiesco) and Brian Mulligan (Paolo) in Giancarlo del Monaco's 1995 production.
date_evidence: Folder '160409 Boccanegra' = 2016-04-09; the tag date is 2016. The MetOpera Database record CID 356423 (re-read by the reconciler) lists Simon Boccanegra at the Metropolitan Opera House, Sat, April 9, 2016 Matinee, as a 'Toll Brothers-Metropolitan Opera International Radio Network Broadcast ... Broadcast live'. It was the only Saturday-matinee radio broadcast in the five-performance run (Apr 1, 5, 9, 13, 16). The Met's Saturday Matinee Broadcasts page (Wayback 2016-04-09) and dated affiliate listings (CapRadio, Red River, Interlochen, WCLV, RTP Antena 2) all advertise it as live on April 9. Met matinee broadcasts are live, so the performance and broadcast dates are the same.
broadcaster: Toll Brothers-Metropolitan Opera International Radio Network (also live on Metropolitan Opera Radio, SiriusXM channel 74; relayed internationally, e.g. RTP Antena 2)
event_name: Met Opera Saturday matinee broadcast (2015-16 season)

program.title: Simon Boccanegra
program.notes: 1881 revised version (libretto Francesco Maria Piave, revised by Arrigo Boito). Prologue and three acts, given with one intermission: Prologue & Act I 93 min; intermission 35 min; Acts II & III 61 min; estimated running time 3 h 9 min (metopera.org). This was the opera's 142nd Met performance.

credits.notes: Interlochen and WCLV listings: her network broadcast debut.
American bass-baritone. No confident Wikidata match.
RTP Antena 2's listing for the 9 April live relay (published 6 April 2016) reads 'Coro e Orquestra do Metropolitan'. The Met archive record does not list ensembles.
Same RTP Antena 2 listing. No source read names the chorus master (see open questions).

AGMAZINE Summer 2016 photo caption: 'Saturday, April 9, 2016, after a performance of Simon Boccanegra at The Metropolitan Opera ... Stage Director Eric Einhorn'. The Met's 1 April 2016 record also lists him as Stage Director.
1995 production, revived. Credited on the Met's production page.
The Met's page of intermission features for this broadcast lists 'Mary Jo Heath interviews Joseph Calleja'. It was the season's only Boccanegra radio broadcast.
Eastman (5 Oct 2015) says she became the Met's radio host in September 2015. No source read names her as host on 9 April itself, but her intermission interview supports it.

credits.notes: Listed on the Met's page of intermission features for this broadcast. Whether both Backstage Pass segments aired in the single intermission, or one aired before or after the opera, is unverified.
Eastman (Oct 2015) names 'Ira Siff on the Saturday matinées' as commentator for the 2015-16 season. No source read names him for 9 April.

open_questions: Track boundaries come from file durations and the Met's published timings (Prologue & Act I 93 min; intermission 35 min; Acts II & III 61 min), not from listening. Files 01-12 (98.8 min) fit the introduction plus Prologue and Act I, file 13 (37.0 min) the intermission, and files 14-21 (67.1 min) Acts II-III plus curtain calls. The Prologue/Act I and Act II/Act III breaks are not pinned. Claude put Act III from file 18 and Codex from file 19; this record follows Claude.

Files 08 and 17 are almost the same length (82.1 s and 82.0 s) but differ in byte size, so they are not file copies. They are taken to be scene-change pauses with host commentary. Only listening can confirm that, or show they are the same filler audio repeated.

Files 01-03 are about 320 kbps and files 04-21 about 128 kbps, with different tag frames (TSOC/composer vs TCM/TSC/TSP). The first 40 minutes may come from a different capture or source (e.g. a SiriusXM or web stream versus FM).

The April 9 Playbill PDF (040916 Boccanegra.pdf) could not be read: the live URL is behind queue-it bot protection and the Wayback Machine has no capture. It would show the chorus master (presumably Donald Palumbo, the Met's chorus director, but no source read says so for this date), and possibly the production staff. The Met's programs page warns that the PDFs leave out late cast changes.

No source records a cast change for April 9. The Met archive record (the authoritative per-date source) lists the same principals as the run's announced cast and notes no replacement. Both researchers found no reviews of the April 9 matinee itself; only opening-night (April 1) reviews were found. The reconciler's web search budget ran out before a further targeted search for substitutions.

The host (Mary Jo Heath) and commentator (Ira Siff) rest on a season-level source (Eastman, Oct 2015). Heath's interview with Calleja is listed for this broadcast. Listening to file 01 would confirm both.

The Met lists four features for this broadcast (two Backstage Pass segments by Loren Toolajian, Heath's interview with Calleja, a Verdi-Boito feature), but it is unverified which aired in the single intermission (file 13) and which, if any, ran before the opera or after it (files 01, 21).
